content:
I'm experimenting with a small "Sorry Atlas" workflow and would love 3–5 Lean files from people who are willing to try it.

The idea is simple:

finished proofs show what Lean already accepts;
sorrys show exactly where mathematical intent is meeting verifier resistance.

I want to see whether unfinished Lean files can be turned into something genuinely useful for the author, not just counted or linted.

If you send me a Lean file with sorries, I'll use my current MathGraph/manual workflow to return a small proof-rescue pack:

  • a short summary of the proof frontier in the file
  • remaining sorries grouped into obstruction families
  • repeated proof obligations compressed into possible helper lemmas
  • likely API / Mathlib gap candidates
  • "this is probably a tactic issue / coercion issue / missing simp lemma / induction motive issue" style diagnoses
  • collaboration-ready proof tasks or Zulip-ready questions
  • easy holes solved where possible

No magic, and no claim that this proves or solves everything. The goal is to learn from the holes.

The only bad sorry is the one that teaches us nothing.

I'll do this manually/experimentally at first, capped at a few files, and I won't share anyone's file or results publicly without permission.

Best candidates are files where:

  • the statements mostly compile
  • the sorries are real proof holes, not placeholders for whole missing theories
  • the project/import context is available enough for me to reproduce the goals
  • you'd actually value a structured diagnosis or proof-roadmap back

A single .lean file is fine if it imports cleanly, a small repo/context is even better if the holes depend on local definitions.

If interested, just reply here or DM me.
